chunks: As for what Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan al-Ṣaffār narrated from Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā, from Sulaymān ibn Ḥafṣ al-Marwazī, from al-Faqīh عليه السلام, who said:

When a man performs hajj, then enters Makkah in tamattuʿ, circles the House, performs two rakʿahs behind the Station of Ibrāhīm عليه السلام, and goes between al-Ṣafā and al-Marwah, then everything becomes lawful for him except women, because for the lawfulness of women there is still upon him a tawaf and a prayer. So this does not contradict what we have mentioned, because there is nothing in the report stating that the tawaf and saʿy after which intercourse is not lawful until after ṭawāf al-nisāʾ are for the ʿumrah or for the hajj. When that is not specified in the report, we interpret it as referring to one who performed tawaf and saʿy for the hajj; thus it is not permissible for him to have intercourse with women. This interpretation is more appropriate, because his saying عليه السلام in the report by way of explanation, 'because for the lawfulness of women there is upon him a tawaf and a prayer,' indicates that. The ʿumrah by which one performs tamattuʿ up to the hajj does not require ṭawāf al-nisāʾ; rather, ṭawāf al-nisāʾ is only obligatory in the separate ʿumrah and the hajj, and that indicates it.

key_terms.السَّعْيَ: the ritual going between al-Ṣafā and al-Marwah
key_terms.الْعُمْرَةِ الْمُفْرَدَةِ: the independent ʿumrah performed separately from hajj tamattuʿ
key_terms.تَحِلَّةِ النِّسَاءِ: the state in which women become lawful again after ihram restrictions
key_terms.طَوَافِ النِّسَاءِ: the tawaf required for the lawfulness of women
key_terms.مَقَامِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ: the Station of Ibrāhīm عليه السلام behind which the two rakʿahs are prayed
key_terms.مُتَمَتِّعًا: performing hajj in the mode of tamattuʿ

ai.seo_question: After completing tawaf and saʿy in ʿumrat al-tamattuʿ, is intercourse with women permissible before ṭawāf al-nisāʾ?
ai.summary: This text addresses a legal ruling concerning one who exits the ihram of ʿumrat al-tamattuʿ and what remains prohibited for him. It explains that marital relations remain forbidden until the required tawaf and prayer connected to the lawfulness of women are completed, and clarifies that ṭawāf al-nisāʾ is not obligatory in ʿumrat al-tamattuʿ but is obligatory in al-ʿumrah al-mufradah and in hajj.
